exposureDisclosure: Fresh independent lecture review. No L33 author keys, solutions, author code/checks or expected computation outputs have been read. An existing isolated toolbox runtime and original installed image assets may be reused; all source transcription and checks are independent.

sourceObservations.observations: Title page: Lecture 33 Image Feature Extraction, printed footer 1. No examinable technical content.
Objective-only page naming region, line and point features; no new technical proposition beyond subsequent content.
Contents map: assumptions, classes; region pixel classification/instances/descriptions; gradients/Canny/Hough; SIFT. No unique technical proposition.

Feature extraction reduces high-dimensional pixels into meaningful repeatable, task-relevant descriptions. Specific uses: localization via distinctive points, grasp boundaries via edges/corners, navigation via obstacle/lane features. Absolute claim that robots cannot operate directly on raw pixels needs qualification for learned internal representations.

Camera-car diagram has raw pixels, then edges, corners, object outline and motion vectors. Text states approximate 10^6–10^8 bytes/s and tens of features/frame, not universal limits. Features may be scalars or vectors answering pose/type/motion tasks. Motion vectors are not object identity labels.

Near/far cube diagram, car occluded by tree, bright/dim red ball, shadow and reflection examples. Pixel size alone lacks metric scale without geometry/camera/depth assumptions; occlusion removes visible region, lighting alters appearance, spurious boundaries need not be actual objects. Reliability depends on assumptions and imperfect classification must be handled later.

Three families: homogeneous contiguous region pixels, geometric straight lines, distinctive repeatable keypoints/corners. Figures show colored robot-workspace regions, corridor line structure, marker corners. A generic keypoint is not necessarily every geometric corner.

Sign input and binary output illustrate partitioning into application-meaningful regions, not complete semantic recognition. Robustness is graceful degradation as assumptions fail, not exact invariance under arbitrary disturbances.

Three stages: pixel classification, instance segmentation, description. Object c=1 and not-object c=0. Otsu minimizes within-class and maximizes between-class variance; class weights matter. Adaptive model explicitly t_uv=mu(W_uv)-k sigma(W_uv), with mean/std and offset parameter. Unique local threshold does not guarantee cleanest target mask.

Actual castle.png example reads float image, sets t=0.7 then overwrites with castle.otsu(), then displays castle>=t. The plotted manual result is a separate comparison, not both produced by that final call. Captions report Otsu 0.6039 and histogram 0.603; histogram line positions also do not line up with those numbers. Adaptive h=15 caption calls window size 15; actual library half-width semantics require independent check. Adaptive result retains strong brick texture, so it is not uniformly cleaner.

Impulse response is L(lambda) times three receptor sensitivities. Primary mixing matrix rows are receptors and columns primary wavelengths; solve p=A^-1 c for invertible A. Displayed p=L A^-1 m equated to matching functions requires stimulus normalization. RGB coefficients encode intensity and chromaticity; r,g,b divide by nonzero sum, sum 1. Numeric wavelengths red 700.0, green 546.1, blue 435.8 nm; mercury-line historical claim is not accepted without evidence. Diagram shows illuminant E, surface reflectance R, outgoing L and eye M.

XYZ imaginary mathematical primaries, normalized x,y,z with nonzero sum and two independent coordinates. Chromaticity normalization loses common magnitude. RGB/XYZ/HSV Euclidean differences do not directly equal perceived differences; Lab designed for improved perceptual uniformity, not a perfect universal metric. Figure contrasts separation in xy versus a*b*.

Color segmentation uses spectral/chromatic properties. Lab a* is green-red, b* blue-yellow; discarding L* emphasizes chromatic rather than lightness variation but does not guarantee arbitrary illuminant invariance. k-means groups color pixels into chosen C classes, not necessarily object instances.

Four yellow targets on gray background. Code reads yellowtargets.png float with sRGB gamma, converts Lab, extracts a*:b*, runs kmeans_color(k=2,seed=0). Two chromatic classes, not two objects. Displayed target class 0 is blue in the false-color map; a*b* centroids are chromatic means, not image locations. Cluster 0 has large positive b*, corresponding to yellow.

Code casts class labels uint8, computes (1-labels)*255, then labels_binary and extracts label 1 top target, label 0 background. Actual four disconnected targets have distinct labels 1–4, background 0. Return count convention needs versioned API check. MSER and graph-based methods are named for complex scenes but no algorithms derived. Geometric instance labels and chromatic class IDs are separate.

Raw moment m_pq=sum u^p v^q X_uv has order p+q. m00 is pixel count only for binary weights 0/1, otherwise weighted mass. Centroid m10/m00,m01/m00 requires nonzero mass. Central moments use offsets from centroid and remove uniform translation, not all scale dependence.

Coordinate second-moment matrix J=[[mu20,mu11],[mu11,mu02]], unlike some mechanical tensor sign/order conventions. mu20=m20-m10^2/m00, mu02=m02-m01^2/m00, mu11=m11-m10*m01/m00. First central moments zero. Equivalent filled ellipse semiaxes 2 sqrt(lambda/m00), major eigenvector for largest eigenvalue. atan(vy/vx) needs quadrant/axis ambiguity qualification; equal eigenvalues have no unique direction. Hu seven invariants need normalized central moments for scale, not central moments alone; raster invariance approximate.

Actual four-blob table: indices 0 bottom, 1 right, 2 left, 3 top. Top centroid (365.7,218.2), area 5.61e3/5609.5, perimeter about309, orientation -87.6 degrees, aspect0.749. Source defines m00 and u20 only, then references u11/u02 without definitions. Missing definitions cause NameError in fresh state. plot_centroid/plot_box operate collection; plot_ellipse with J3 plots one ellipse, despite displayed four-ellipse figure. Fractional contour area differs from binary pixel counting. Original top connected label1 is not blob index3.

Boundary edgels can be encoded as chain directions, requiring a start for absolute location. Circularity rho=4*pi*A/P^2 gives circle1, square pi/4 and ideal uniform-scale invariance. Radius signature is centroid-to-boundary distance sequence; raw indexwise comparison is not rotation invariant without phase alignment or suitable invariant matching.

Source literal first call blobs[0].polar contradicts caption naming blob3. r and angle are plotted against sample index, not physical time. Each radius profile normalized by r.sum removes common scale only under consistent sampling. polarmatch(1) compares against blob1; exact returned offset semantics need API check. perimeter.shape is array dimensions, not metric length. Orange perimeter plot explicitly uses blobs[3].plot_perimeter, which does match top target caption.

Learned feature pipeline explicitly named, qualifying page990 raw-pixel overstatement. Actual figure depicts detection boxes/classes around people, bicycles, cars, motorcycle, dog. Text conflates Faster R-CNN detection with pixel/instance masks; standard Mask R-CNN supplies a separate mask branch. Eighty COCO categories are this training vocabulary, not universal architecture limit. No executable detector code here.

Street image beside line drawing retains selected geometric structure, omits much original texture/color and does not provide metric depth. Straight boundaries especially common in built environments. Diagram includes roads, buildings and poles.

Image derivatives via convolution; smoothing reduces amplified noise. Associativity combines derivative kernel and Gaussian under compatible boundary/convolution conventions. Magnitude sqrt(Iu^2+Iv^2), direction atan2(Iv,Iu). Diagram smoothing then derivatives then magnitude/direction. Euclidean theoretical magnitude is distinct from some API default approximations.

Canny stages: gradient estimation, nonmaximum suppression across edge along gradient, then high/low hysteresis. Weak values retained only if connected to a strong response through eligible chain. Figures illustrate local across-ridge maximum and high/low levels; arbitrary equality conventions need explicit assumptions.

Polar Hough line rho=u cos(theta)+v sin(theta); theta is normal angle, rho signed perpendicular offset under parameter convention. Polar form handles vertical lines. Each edgel votes along candidate parameter curve; common intersections accumulate. Quantization and discontinuous edgels mean a peak does not prove an unbroken physical boundary.

Five-point image and accumulator show horizontal bottom pair with two votes and rising-image diagonal through three points. Supplied idealized coordinates in Q058 avoid inferring exact raster coordinates. Code reads 5points.png, Hough, lines(2) with comment min votes3, selects lines[0], plot_lines. Additional lines(1) plot yields more candidates. Strict versus inclusive Hough threshold must be checked against installed implementation, not assume caption is typo.

Church source reads mono image, to_int, GaussianBlur(img,(5,5),1.4), Canny(smooth,50,100), wraps Image, Hough, lines_p(100,minlinelength=200,maxlinegap=5,seed=0). Thus integer conversion precedes smoothing, edges precede line segments. Default norm for Canny needs API check; thresholds are not original color labels. Figure shows selected long church boundaries; no claim all edge pixels become segments.

Harris A averages gradient products, not products of mean gradients. Source calls Iu,Iv derivatives of Gaussian but should mean image gradients computed with such kernels, not bare kernels. Both eigenvalues small flat, one large edge, both substantial corner. C=det(A)-alpha trace(A)^2. Generic claim all interest points robust to scale needs qualification for fixed-scale Harris.

Scale-space 3D u,v,sigma; DoG subtracts nearby Gaussian-smoothed levels and approximates a proportional scale-normalized LoG, not arbitrary unnormalized equality. Candidate compares eight same-level neighbors plus nine each adjacent level, total26. Extrema are candidates pending stability/localization, not guaranteed matches. Scale can change corner appearance to edge.

SIFT stage order: extrema, localization/stability, dominant orientation, descriptor. Displayed 16x16 patch divided into4x4 cells, each8 orientation bins =>128 values. Separate orientation-assignment histogram should not be equated with8 descriptor bins. Text does not show normalization/clipping or matching ratio rule, so those require explicit external premises if introduced.

Source reads building2-1.png mono. Harris(nfeat=500) plots crosses. SIFT().filter(percentstrength=50,minscale=5) plots circles/scales and hand orientations. Comment top50 percent strength is not necessarily half the keypoint count; exact filter compares to maximum and threshold equality needs installed check. Larger scale minimum is explicitly5 pixels. No second view/matches or object boxes in the overlay.

Summary repeats region/line/point roles, assumptions and descriptor examples. It groups Harris with scale-invariant SIFT too broadly; ordinary fixed-scale Harris is not inherently scale invariant. No new mathematical model, but this source conflict is substantive and cited.
Reference list only: Szeliski, Corke, Forsyth. No new examinable technical claims; bibliographic details not treated as assessment content.
Thank-you only, printed footer34. No examinable content.

independentAnswers.reasoning: Feature extraction reduces the representation while retaining information useful for the specified downstream task; it need not retain every pixel exactly.
Page 1007 explicitly allows learned internal features from pixel inputs, qualifying the absolute introductory wording without eliminating data or task assumptions.
The actual diagram associates edges/outlines with boundary geometry, corners with distinctive locations, and motion vectors with temporal displacement.
The near/far projection illustration shows that pixel extent alone lacks metric scale; camera and geometric/depth assumptions are required.
The tree hides part of the car without changing its true size, and different lighting changes the observed ball appearance.
A homogeneous patch is a region, a straight corridor boundary a line, and a distinctive corner a point feature.
Segmentation partitions meaningful regions; source robustness is graceful degradation when assumptions fail, not unlimited exact invariance or letter recognition.
Pixel class assignment precedes separating spatial instances and then describing their area/centroid.
Otsu compares class-probability-weighted within-class variance, equivalently between-class variance, not medians or component counts.
The supplied local rule gives 120-0.5*20=110; intensity 115 is foreground under the stated >= convention.
The second assignment overwrites t=0.7; the final comparison uses the computed Otsu threshold.

The supplied API premise is independently confirmed in installed toolbox 2.4.1: h=15 gives width 2h+1=31 and default threshold is local mean minus C, not the separate mean-minus-k-standard-deviation model.
Both actual slide and independent castle output show substantial brick texture in the adaptive mask. This disproves guaranteed cleanest-target interpretation, not the usefulness of adaptation.
Multiply each sensitivity by the supplied stimulus 2: (0.4,1.0,0.2).
Primary mixing is A p=c with the specified receptor-row convention; invertibility gives p=A^-1 c.
Divide by total 10 to obtain (0.2,0.3,0.5); common positive scaling doubles numerator and denominator and cancels.
The arbitrary stimulus magnitude multiplies the primary coefficients; unit-stimulus matching functions require a fixed normalization.
Printed numeric primaries are red700.0, green546.1, blue435.8 nm. The diagram shows illuminant and surface reflectance affecting the eye input; the mercury-line historical claim is not endorsed.
XYZ mathematical primaries are not required to be physically realizable lamps; Lab is designed to improve perceptual uniformity rather than remove all observer/illumination effects.
Dividing by nonzero X+Y+Z gives x+y+z=1 and therefore z=1-x-y, while the original common magnitude is lost.
Discarding L* emphasizes chromatic coordinates a*,b*, not spatial location, and neither fixes k nor guarantees arbitrary illumination invariance.
The source labels a* green-to-red and b* blue-to-yellow.
The image has four separate targets but k=2 groups their pixels into two chromatic classes, yellow versus gray.
Centroids plotted on a*b* axes are means of color clusters, not image-space centroids or metric grasp positions.
The blue rendering is a false-color class map. Class0 is nominal, not a statement that the original target was blue or always has that ID.
For label0, (1-0)*255=255; for label1, (1-1)*255=0. Independent uint8 calculation confirms.
Four foreground components plus background give N=5, with labels0 through4; installed labels_binary and original target execution agree.
The two diagonal pixels do not touch in four-neighbor connectivity but do in eight-neighbor connectivity; foreground counts are two and one.
The zeroth moment sums weights; it equals pixel count only when foreground weights are1 and background0.
Moment order is p+q=2+1=3; centering removes a uniform coordinate translation, not arbitrary scale changes.
Semiaxes are 2sqrt(100/25)=4 and 2sqrt(25/25)=2; minor/major=0.5.
Eigenvalues of [[5,2],[2,5]] are7 and3; the major eigenvector is proportional to(1,1). With mass4, semiaxes are sqrt7 and sqrt3.
atan2 handles quadrant/vertical cases, an unoriented axis is modulo pi, and repeated eigenvalues do not define a unique major axis.

Hu descriptors use normalized central moments through degree3. Centering and scale normalization are different operations; discretization and finite precision limit exact raster invariance. Unnormalized arbitrary moments are not scale invariant.
Python evaluates the undefined u11 first; NumPy cannot infer it or u02 from m00. Independent execution of the literal incomplete expression raises NameError.
Actual table row3 matches the top target at image coordinates roughly365.7,218.2, near vertical and aspect0.749. Runtime gives the equivalent axis modulo pi; it is not an a*b* point.
Connected-components labels and contour-blob indices enumerate independently. The top object is source label1 and blob3, independently reproduced.
Contour polygon area can be fractional. The executed top object has contour area5609.5 but 5762 foreground raster pixels, so the two area conventions differ.
The steps have lengths1,1,sqrt2,1, total3+sqrt2. A starting pixel anchors the directional sequence to absolute position.
Circle area pi*r^2 and perimeter2*pi*r yield1; square area s^2 and perimeter4s yield pi/4, independent of size.
Uniform scale3 gives area factor9 and perimeter factor3, whose square cancels the area factor in circularity.
Radius profiles can be cyclically phase shifted by rotation or a changed boundary start. Common amplitude normalization alone does not align indices.
The executable call explicitly selects blobs[0]; a caption naming3 does not change the index. The later perimeter plot of blob3 is a separate call.
With consistent sampling, r/r.sum cancels a common scale. Installed polarmatch cross-correlates normalized profiles against target index1 and returns similarity plus an orientation offset.
perimeter.shape is the dimensions of a 2-by-N coordinate array, while perimeter_length is a scalar Euclidean boundary length; executed top example is(2,303) and about309.04.
The inspected figure shows detections. The original Mask R-CNN paper adds a mask branch to Faster R-CNN detection, so a bounding box is not an instance mask.
Eighty categories describe the particular pretrained COCO vocabulary, not a universal class-count limit or contents of each image.
The line drawing retains selected boundary geometry while omitting much color/texture; it is not reversible original data or metric depth.
sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 and atan2(4,3)=53.13 degrees from +u.
Associativity combines smoothing and derivative filtering under compatible convolution/boundary conventions; it does not make distinct kernels identical.
Nonmaximum suppression compares gradient magnitude along the gradient direction, across the edge rather than along its tangent.
The12 response seeds the eligible8-6 chain; an isolated8 has no connection to a strong pixel and is discarded.
In the displayed polar equation the unit normal is(cos theta,sin theta); theta is its angle from +u.
At theta0 the equation reduces to rho=u, so the vertical line u=6 has rho6.
Collinear edgels have candidate curves intersecting at a shared rho/theta bin. Quantized support does not establish a continuous unbroken edge.
The points(39,9),(24,24),(9,39) satisfy u+v=48; only(9,39),(39,39) satisfy v=39.
The literal code order is integer grayscale, Gaussian blur, Canny edge map, then probabilistic Hough segments.
The parameter names and installed wrapper define minimum line length200 and maximum linked gap5 in pixel coordinates.
Independent official documentation and actual execution confirm default Canny matches explicit L2gradient=False, using L1 rather than the theory-page Euclidean magnitude.
Harris averages the products Iu^2,IuIv,Iv^2 using the local window; it does not first average gradients or use bare derivative kernels as image responses.
A corner changes significantly in two independent local directions, hence both structure-matrix eigenvalues substantial; one large implies edge, two small flat.
Ordinary fixed-scale Harris lacks explicit scale-space search, whereas SIFT searches characteristic scale. The source summary is overbroad.
For nearby scales, Gaussian differences approximate a factor times sigma^2 Laplacian(G); the scale normalization and ratio factor matter.
There are8 same-level neighbors plus9 below and9 above, excluding the candidate itself, total26.
A scale-space extremum is only a candidate before localization and stability/contrast/edge-response tests, not guaranteed unique recognition.
The displayed order is extrema detection, localization, orientation assignment, descriptor construction.
Four-by-four spatial cells give16 histograms times8 orientation bins=128 descriptor components.
Eight bins per descriptor cell do not specify the separate dominant-orientation histogram; the original SIFT paper uses a distinct36-bin assignment histogram.
Half maximum strength is5; A and C meet both inclusive strength>=5 and scale>=5, while B fails scale and D fails strength.
The actual SIFT overlay uses circles and radial hands for scale and orientation; Harris crosses indicate locations, not object boxes or second-image matches.
Different tasks require different representations: spatial target regions/instances, wall lines, and repeatable point descriptors; color class alone does not identify all instances.
The stated strict OpenCV condition votes>2 requires at least3 integer votes. Official docs and an independent three-pixel control confirm, despite the wrapper docstring using loose at-least wording.
Expand the central first moment: sum uX-u_c sum X=m10-(m10/m00)m00=0 for nonzero mass.
The collection methods plot all centroids and boxes; only one plot_ellipse call uses the single J3 and centroid3. The displayed four-ellipse image is broader than the literal snippet.

status: 77 independent answers and computations frozen before keys

externalEvidence.qualification: Official adaptive-threshold API: half-width and local mean minus C; independently corroborated by installed2.4.1 implementation and runtime.
Official polar-match API describes target index, cross-correlation, similarity and orientation offset. Installed implementation and original-image self-match checked.
Official primary API states default Canny L1 and standard Hough strict vote threshold; independently tested in installed OpenCV5.0.0.93.
Official Hu formulas use normalized moments; contour geometry differs from raster sums.
Original SIFT paper confirms normalized-LoG relation, separate36-bin orientation assignment and scale-space design. No claim of perfect invariance to arbitrary viewpoint changes.
Original Mask R-CNN paper explicitly adds an instance-mask branch to Faster R-CNN detection.

Blob top orientation in current runtime is+92.3987 degrees, equivalent modulo180 degrees to printed-87.6 degrees.
